traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md are implemented and verified: - Core Functionality: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport implement detection, update, batch, verification, and reporting, with matching CLI commands. Tests cover both logic and CLI behavior. - Quality Standards: Operations are conservative (only @story text replacement, files only written when changed, no runtime behavior or non-comment code altered). Detection and reporting are read-only. Tests confirm updates happen where expected and that dry-run mode is non-destructive. - Integration: Maintenance API is exported via the plugin’s main entrypoint (src/index.ts) as `maintenance`, and a `traceability-maint` CLI is wired via the `bin` field in package.json. Tests verify index exports and CLI integration end-to-end. - User Experience: CLI outputs clear, human-readable messages and structured JSON where appropriate, including summaries, counts, and helpful guidance. Help text describes commands and options. Tests assert on these messages. - Error Handling: The code handles non-existent roots, permission errors, invalid flags (e.g., --format yaml), unsafe story paths, and unexpected exceptions gracefully, using distinct exit codes and prefixed error messages. Tests explicitly cover these cases. - Documentation: The Maintenance API and CLI are fully documented in user-docs/api-reference.md and referenced from README.md, including usage examples, output formats, and behavior notes.
Given the comprehensive implementation, passing tests tied directly to this story, and user-facing documentation, the story is fully satisfied.
